title: FPGA Design Agent
tagline: An agentic FPGA design environment: from a plain-English request to a bitstream proven on the board
description: Language-model agents turn a plain-English request into a spec, tests and SystemVerilog, then drive the simulators and Vivado 2026.1 to a bitstream on a Digilent Nexys A7, with every stage judged by checks run in code, hidden tests and the board.

facts.text: 13 of 21 development runs passed every hidden test (Anthropic Claude Sonnet, claude-sonnet-5-5, through Claude Code; development tasks, not a held-out score).
282 deliberate bugs planted across the benchmark's development tasks, every one caught by the hidden tests: a check on the benchmark itself, not an agent result.

On four small tasks, run up to simulation with one low-cost model, a harness change that moves large tool results to a file cut cost per run by 32.8 % (95 % interval 4.3 % to 53.3 %) with the same hidden-test passes; not adopted, as the pre-registered rule did not say whether cost alone counts.

media.alt: The agent's feedback loop on the bench, replayed from a recorded run: role agents, simulators, Vivado 2026.1, the Nexys A7 board and the instruments, each returning a result to a gate.
media.note: The loop replay animates one recorded run; the labels on its arrows come from several recorded runs, named on the site.

made_from: site/public/index.html (the loop replay and the runs chart), captured by puppeteer; see README.md
status: Proven on the board so far for the hand-built reference design; the one agent-built design programmed so far passed 3 of 3 serial-link tests and failed its logic-analyser captures. No held-out score yet.
